A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Policy Contrastive Decoding for Robotic Foundation Models. All 21 pages, including Appendices A–L, support reliable comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: v5 reports original simulation and real-world experiments in Table 1 and Figure 3, plus original supplementary experiments, including LIBERO-90 results in Appendix K.

after.justification: v6 retains these original simulation, real-world, and supplementary experimental results, including Table 1, Figure 3, and Appendix K.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the identical PCD procedure, Track2Mask component, KDE-based probabilistic modeling, and inference steps.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same nine SIMPLER tasks, six real-world tasks, five sampled LIBERO-90 tasks, and scene-variation scenarios. No task, dataset, or domain coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: OpenVLA, Octo, and π0 in Table 1; CFG in Table 6; and miniVLA+VQ h8+Wrist in Table 11.

E3.justification: Both retain 300 trials per simulation task, 20 trials per real-world task, identical π0 finetuning settings, and the same evaluation metrics and supplementary testing procedures.

E4.justification: The design ablations and scene-variation tests in Sections 4.3–4.4 are identical. Appendix analyses of maximum-step performance, CFG timing, masking failures, multi-object masking, and distractor robustness are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain the same 95% confidence-interval reporting. Trial counts and all other statistical reporting remain unchanged, with no added seed information or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 11 retains average scores of 71.2 for miniVLA+VQ h8+Wrist and 79.6 with PCD in both versions.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Equations (1)–(3), and the action-dimension independence assumption are identical. No mathematical definitions, reasoning, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free mitigation of spurious correlations, compatibility with autoregressive and diffusion-based policies, and experimental effectiveness.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including computational overhead, the focus on inference rather than training, Track2Mask failure conditions, and task-dependent annotation effectiveness.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, Table 2 hyperparameters, robot hardware, computational costs, and project and baseline access links are unchanged. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning are identical, including the relationship to visual contrastive decoding in Section 2 and classifier-free guidance in Appendix F.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Accepted' to 'Published' as a conference paper at ICLR 2026, and the arXiv version/date stamp updates. The acknowledgment replaces 'Natural Science Foundation of Sichuan Province' with 'Sichuan Science and Technology Program', retaining grant No.2026NSFSC1479. Other prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11, Tables 1–11, and Algorithm 1 retain identical displays and placement. Rendered-page differences are confined to the textual edits identified under P1; page layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 updates publication information and a funding-program name, while preserving the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and visual presentation. These administrative edits establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
